rv.q: It is a vision of love, guttering in the void; a strange dream ofAmerica, falling through the night.
John Tiffany's staging of this intense episode is alone worth the price of a ticket.
I loathe The Glass Menagerie — and did so the first time I saw it as a teenager — yet this is a strong rendition of the play, should your taste run to claustrophobic glumness.
This long scene is worth the price of admission alone as Brian J Smith and Kate O'Flynn convey an aching tenderness and mutual generosity that only makes the conclusion more poignant.
Nevertheless, the pain and the humour of Williams’s writing shine through by dint of three splendid performances.

cn.t: Critics praise this production of Williams' classic memory play, with Cherry Jones earning particular acclaim for her formidable portrayal of overbearing matriarch Amanda alongside strong performances from the entire cast.
